cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Challenge by Proxy
cards.instruction: Persuade someone else to challenge a rule or authority before you risk doing it yourself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Ask the director why the overtime rule changed. I'll support you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Your fresh perspective won't carry my disciplinary history.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Just behind. Where supportive people remain employable.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 directs the challenge, A3 postpones B why-me question while assigning risk, and A5 approves support only behind B rather than beside.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 asks A to challenge personally; A3 cites disciplinary risk; B4 asks equal visible support, causing A5 reduced exposure.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 reasonably ask A to share the challenge, giving the proxy recruitment a credible negotiation.

heightening.evidence: B4 solidarity request becomes A5 a carefully limited physical role that keeps B first.

specificity.evidence: A1 director and overtime rule, A3 disciplinary history establish the authority and A perceived risk.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 supportive-people-remain-employable is earned by B4 requested position and the stated disciplinary concern.

A1-B2.evidence: A1 asks B to challenge overtime; B2 asks why A will not.

B2-A3.evidence: A3 responds to B2 with lower-risk B history and defers further questioning.

A3-B4.evidence: A3 risk distinction causes B4 to request side-by-side support.
